project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Develop and demonstrate a clean technology value chain that is close enough to market to support industrial deployment.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Choose one main clean technology area and demonstrate an integrated value chain. The areas cover energy systems, zero-emission power, and storage, renewable fuels or use of captured carbon.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope
R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Clean Technologies for Climate Action · Topic Q&A 96065

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Clean technology suppliers and users need reliable systems that approach market readiness and deliver lower-cost energy with lower emissions.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Deliver a demonstrator with realistic performance evidence, detailed engineering, permits and a credible business and market-readiness plan before deciding whether to build.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Show measurable emissions cuts, more use of recycled or reused materials and lower lifetime energy costs. Explain how the value chain strengthens European industrial capability.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Expected Outcome
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Prepare a business plan and market-readiness strategy that identify deployment barriers, industrial partners who will lead deployment and the route to financing and repeat use.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The proposal needs at least three independent funded partners in three different eligible countries. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme). The call recommends no more than ten participants and expects applicants to justify the size based on their value chain.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: Build an industry-driven group along the chosen clean technology value chain. Involving small and medium-sized enterprises is encouraged. Include the partners that can lead deployment after the grant.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer: Justify the consortium size and allocate responsibilities across the value chain. Identify which industrial partners will lead deployment and who will produce the evidence needed for the decision to build.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on integrated clean technology and represent it to the funder. The topic expects an industry-driven consortium and asks it to identify industrial deployment leads.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate only if the proposal can show industry-led delivery and a credible route to deployment. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder). The consortium should be industry driven, with a manageable size and an identified lead for eventual deployment.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could take part in integrated clean technology without receiving a grant. As an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant), it could validate an electricity-grid interface as part of the integrated clean technology value chain. It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could validate an electricity-grid interface as part of the integrated clean technology value chain. Budget at least 30% of those costs from other resources. The topic excludes organisations directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established there.

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could validate grid interfaces or flexibility in a demonstration that integrates clean electricity with industry. Its role would need to serve the selected value chain.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: Develop an innovative technological solution. Its demonstration should show that the complete value chain works and can move towards industrial use.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Innovation can be in integrated energy networks and systems, zero-emission power, energy storage, renewable fuels or use of captured carbon.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Design and integrate the clean technology, then prepare one or more demonstrations. Include a decision point before contracting and building the demonstrator.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 8 (technology readiness level: a complete, qualified system) by project end. The work is expected to start at TRL 6 (technology readiness level: technology demonstrated in a relevant setting).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Specific conditions

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Demonstrate the integrated technology in a relevant setting and plan a decision before contracting and construction. The decision requires evidence including engineering, permits and a viable implementation plan.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Connect technology suppliers, users and other value-chain actors around a single main area. Show how its components work together and how industry will deploy the result.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Use realistic baselines to assess emissions, energy costs and use of circular materials. Before construction, provide permits, detailed engineering and a business and market-readiness plan.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: Industrial partners should lead deployment and the consortium should address downstream users’ needs. Identify the industrial partners that will take the solution to market.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 140 million for integrated clean technology. It expects 8 awards.
- Grant request: EUR 15–25 million per project is indicative. The Commission can select a different request.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · p. 8 · Overview of this call
R&I in Support of the Clean Industrial Deal: Clean Technologies for Climate Action · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards integrated clean technology.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Horizontal Activities · pp. 40–43 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Plan the budget for integrated clean technology using the cost categories allowed by the grant. The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) specifies how those costs can be claimed.
- Eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow): Personnel, purchases and eligible subcontracting.
- Overheads and value added tax (tax on purchases): The indirect-cost rate (overheads such as general office expenses) is 25% of the eligible direct-cost base after exclusions. value added tax is eligible where it is unrecoverable and the cost otherwise qualifies.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 32 · Budget categories and cost eligibility rules

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for integrated clean technology around the initial advance and later payments.
- Payment model: Usually pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant), then interim payments linked to reporting and a final balance.
- Retention or guarantee: 5–8% of the maximum grant is deducted from pre-financing for the mutual insurance mechanism (a common fund covering grant recovery risks).

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for integrated clean technology through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 15 September 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal). Part B is limited to 60 pages.
- Opening: 12 January 2027.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for integrated clean technology.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting integrated clean technology is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around five months after the deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): The indicative signature date is around eight months after the deadline.

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The clean-technology application needs a business plan and market-readiness strategy within its plan for sharing and using results.
- Application form: Complete Part A online and upload Part B as a fixed-format document with the required annexes.
- Registration: Enter a participant identification code for each beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entity (organisations legally linked to funded partners).
- Plan: Include a business plan and market-readiness strategy in the draft dissemination, exploitation and communication plan.
cards.sources:

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Integrated clean technology proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation.
- Thresholds: At least 3/5 per criterion and 10/15 overall.
- Weighting: Impact is multiplied by 1.5 for the ranking.
- Ranking rules: Technology portfolio: At least the top-ranked proposal in each main area is selected if it clears all thresholds.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Check component sourcing conditions and readiness evidence for the proposed clean-technology demonstration.
- Conditional — Component dependence: For components flagged under the Net-Zero Industry Act for over 50% dependence on one third country, source at least 50% in eligible European Union or associated countries, or justify a lower share.
- Conditional — Satellite services: Use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing for satellite-based observation, positioning, navigation or timing.
- Exception — Ownership and control: Entities directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established in China cannot participate.
- Exception — Transfer of results: The granting authority may object to a transfer of ownership or to exclusive licensing (giving another party sole rights to use the results) for up to four years after the project ends.
